input.quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Substance is at or above the fallback, but the affiliates element is carried only by inference, so I am flagging this for reviewer sign-off rather than asserting clean compliance, and attaching an optional clarifying redline. What the clause already achieves: § 4(c) (p0021) grants a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual licence of Contractor's Information, with no revocation or at-will termination mechanic anywhere (§ 6 termination at p0032-p0033 contains no licence clawback), and a broad use scope ("in connection with Company's business operations") rather than internal use only. Affiliates and contractors are never named in the agreement - the word "Affiliate" appears nowhere - so coverage depends on reading the unconditional "right to grant a sublicense" as a self-executing path to extend the licence to affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf. That reading defeats the walk-away trigger (excluded with no path to add them) and is at least as favourable as the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice), but it is a phrasing variant rather than express words, which is why this is needs_review. The proposed edit is a drafting clarification of the existing bargain, not a scope grab: it names our Affiliates and contractors as licensees, adds the express "irrevocable" label to match the existing perpetuity, and confirms transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition (today left to the mutual § 10 nonassignability clause at p0042, where consent "will not be unreasonably withheld"). The grant runs in our favour (Company = Clear Capital; Contractor = RadialSpark), so this is not a deviation to be pressed hard - if RadialSpark resists, the fallback of adding affiliates on written notice, or leaving § 4(c) as drafted, remains acceptable.

proposal.summary: Name Clear Capital's affiliates and contractors as licensees in § 4(c), label the licence irrevocable, and confirm transfer to a successor in a merger or acquisition.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We named our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf as licensees and confirmed the licence is irrevocable and transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition, so that operational use across our group does not depend on inferring it from the sublicensing right. This is a drafting clarification of the existing bargain, not a change in scope; if you prefer, we can instead add affiliates on written notice.

ops.oldText: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense)
ops.newText: Contractor hereby grants to Company, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf a royalty-free, non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense and the right to transfer this license to a successor in a merger or acquisition)
